extracted.intended_audience: EPA decisionmakers, agency counsel, environmental lawyers, and reviewing courts
extracted.subtask_description: A formal legal notice-and-comment brief arguing that EPA’s proposed reconsideration/repeal of the Endangerment Finding violates administrative law, statutory rulemaking procedures, and scientific-integrity/FACA requirements. The document identifies the legal and evidentiary standards EPA must meet and explains how the proposal fails those standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on legally and analytically flawed or biased reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Any utilization of the legally and analytically flawed and biased Draft CWG Report by EPA—including in this and other rulemaking proceedings, environmental review documents, permit proceedings, or other agency action—would be arbitrary and capricious and unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency action is unlawful if it relies on faulty or biased data, fails to appropriately consider countervailing evidence, or “rests upon a factual premise that is unsupported by substantial evidence.” Examples/case law cited: Flyers Rights Education Fund v. FAA; Tex. Oil & Gas Ass'n v. EPA; New Orleans v. SEC; Humana of Aurora v. Heckler; Almay, Inc. v. Califano; American Petroleum Institute v. EPA (biased analysis); Genuine Parts Co. v. EPA. The brief identifies specific flaws: lack of independent peer review, noncompliance with EPA/DOE/OMB guidance, and FACA violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoned decisionmaking and substantial-evidence requirement for deference
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts defer to an agency’s expertise only when its decision is supported by substantial evidence in the record and reached by reasoned decisionmaking, including an examination of relevant data and a stated connection between the facts found and the choice made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Stingray Pipeline Co. v. FERC; Pub. Citizen Health Rsch. Grp. v. Tyson; K N Energy v. FERC. Guidance emphasizes that EPA must examine relevant data and provide a reasoned explanation linking facts to its choice; where the agency fails to exercise its expertise or relies on an overtly flawed report, deference does not attach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with scientific integrity guidance and FACA (transparency and fair-balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must follow long-standing internal guidelines designed to ensure it relies on quality science untainted by politically driven outcomes and must comply with FACA’s transparency and fair-balance requirements when using outside committees/reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Draft CWG Report is criticized for never receiving independent peer review, not complying with EPA, DOE, or OMB guidance on use and evaluation of scientific information, and being created in violation of FACA. An agency relying on outside scientific inputs must ensure those inputs meet applicable peer-review, transparency, and balance standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and respond to countervailing evidence before adopting conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency cannot refuse to consider empirical evidence supporting a different approach or ignore evidence that runs counter to its decision; failing to address important contrary facts renders action arbitrary and capricious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Am. Radio Relay League v. FCC; Genuine Parts Co. v. EPA; State Farm. Guidance: EPA must address the 'overwhelming majority' of scientific evidence contradicting the Draft CWG Report before relying on it; must explain why it prioritizes one report over a broad body of conflicting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: More detailed justification required when reversing prior policy (Fox standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency reverses a policy that was supported by prior factual findings, it must provide a more detailed justification than would suffice for a new policy written on a blank slate and cannot ignore matters that underlay the prior policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites FCC v. Fox Television Stations. The proposal must explain disregarding facts and circumstances that underlay the prior Endangerment Finding and engage with decades of supporting scientific evidence; mere reduced confidence is insufficient to justify reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed rule must include statement of basis and purpose (42 U.S.C. §7607(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule must be accompanied by a statement of its basis and purpose summarizing: (A) the factual data on which the proposed rule is based; (B) the methodology used in obtaining and analyzing the data; and (C) the major legal interpretations and policy considerations underlying the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a statutory requirement for Clean Air Act rulemakings; failure to include these elements undermines the proposal’s validity. See 42 U.S.C. §7607(d)(3) and related Clean Air Act and APA review standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement to set forth or reference National Academy findings and explain deviations (42 U.S.C. §7607(d)(3)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of basis and purpose must set forth or summarize and provide a reference to pertinent findings, recommendations, and comments by the National Academy of Sciences, and if the proposal differs from those recommendations, an explanation of the reasons for such differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must include in the docket, on the date of publication, all data, information, and documents referred to. The brief notes EPA failed to cite or reference NAS reviews relevant to NCA5 and the Endangerment Finding, violating this statutory duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rule obligations: respond to significant comments and rely only on docketed information (42 U.S.C. §7607(d)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A promulgated rule must be accompanied by a statement of basis and purpose and an explanation of major changes, and must include a response to each significant comment, criticism, and new data submitted during the comment period; the rule may not be based on information not placed in the docket as of promulgation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Section 307(d)(6) and explains final-rule obligations to respond and to rely only on docketed materials. Failure to respond to significant comments or to place relied-upon information in the docket is a legal defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not disregard high-quality assessments (National Climate Assessment, IPCC) without valid reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA cannot lawfully disregard the congressionally mandated National Climate Assessments and IPCC reports, which are high-quality sources reflecting overwhelming scientific consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Endangerment Finding previously relied on NCA and IPCC material and concluded those processes were robust and consistent with OMB Information Quality Act guidance. The proposal’s reliance on unnamed watchdog concerns to disregard these assessments is insufficient; criticisms must be substantive and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency: apply standards uniformly across sources
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency’s actions must be consistent; internally inconsistent analyses—e.g., applying alleged information-quality defects to the National Climate Assessment but not evaluating the DOE Draft CWG Report by the same standards—are arbitrary and capricious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Nat’l Parks Conservation Ass’n v. EPA and ANR Storage Co. v. FERC. EPA must reconcile inconsistencies and apply evaluation standards uniformly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurately present scientific uncertainties and avoid cherry-picking
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency must not selectively quote or misrepresent prior findings or uncertainties; uncertainties must be presented with appropriate context and explanation rather than used to imply unwarranted conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: the proposed reconsideration selectively quotes the Endangerment Finding’s acknowledgment of varying certainty; it misrepresents sea-level evidence by cherry-picking tide gauges rather than relying on comprehensive satellite altimetry. The agency must explain uncertainty in context and not use selective presentation to overturn prior conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertain accuracy of underlying data before relying on a study
rubrics_metrics.description: Before relying on a report or study, the agency must ascertain the accuracy of the data underlying it; reliance on a report without ascertaining data accuracy can render action arbitrary and capricious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites New Orleans v. SEC, Flyers Rights, and related cases. The brief highlights that reliance on a report without verifying data accuracy or independent peer review (as with the Draft CWG Report) is legally defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate cumulative weight of scientific evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency decisionmaking should consider the cumulative effect of supporting and opposing studies to determine whether the totality of evidence provides a rational basis for action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Ethyl Corp. v. EPA: scientific evidence is cumulative and courts evaluate whether, after considering inferences from both supporting and opposing studies, the cumulative effect presents a rational basis for agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to review and consider comments in other agency dockets when relying on those materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If EPA relies on a report produced or docketed by another agency (e.g., the DOE Draft CWG Report), it must consider and respond to the comments submitted in that other agency’s docket, and must not treat those comments as invisible or unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical example: as of close of EPA comment period only 345 of 59,563 comments submitted to regulations.gov on the Draft CWG Report were publicly available; EPA must conduct its own evaluation of public input in both the DOE docket and its own if it intends to rely on the report in a final rule.
